Irritable behavior, angry outbursts, or acting aggressively

vignette: Alejandro's fingers trembled as he grasped his guitar, the familiar weight and feel of it offering little solace. It had been years since the night that changed everything, yet the memories still lingered, fragmented and terrifying. He was a musician, known for his passionate performances, but lately, even the thought of taking the stage made him anxious. That fateful evening, Alejandro had been walking home from a gig when he was confronted by a group of men who dragged him into an alleyway. The assault that followed left him shattered, both physically and emotionally. The smell of cologne still transported him back to that moment, his heart racing as if it was happening all over again. He couldn't explain why this particular scent was so potent, but the association was unshakeable. As time passed, Alejandro began to suppress his anger, fearful of losing control like he had that night. His wife noticed a change in him, commenting on how distant and withdrawn he'd become. But Alejandro couldn't allow himself to feel or express his emotions, afraid of unleashing a torrent of rage that might consume him whole. When his bandmates tried to bring up the past, he shut them down, insisting they focus on the music instead. Alejandro's world began to shrink as he avoided people in authority, like police officers and even security guards at concerts. He couldn't shake off the feeling that anyone in a uniform was a potential threat. His social circle dwindled as well; seeing old friends brought back too many memories of the night before the assault, when life had been carefree and joyful. Now, those same faces seemed to mock him with their happiness. Alejandro's perception of safety narrowed dramatically. He only felt secure in his own home, where he could control every detail. Even then, sudden movements by others put him on high alert; a careless gesture or unexpected sound made him flinch. His irritability escalated, manifesting in angry outbursts that left those around him bewildered. Alejandro's recollections of the assault remained stubbornly incomplete. He'd catch glimpses of himself trying to fight back, but the memory would dissolve before he could grasp it fully. Some moments were crystal clear - the smell of cologne, the sound of his own screams - while others were shrouded in darkness. When asked about that night, Alejandro struggled to piece together a coherent story; the narrative broke apart like shattered glass. One thing was certain: Alejandro couldn't keep living this way. His relationships were suffering, his music had become stale and forced, and he felt perpetually trapped. The weight of his secret threatened to consume him whole. With a sense of trepidation, Alejandro made an appointment with a therapist, unsure what the future held but desperate for some semblance of peace. As he sat in the waiting room, fidgeting with the strap on his guitar case, Alejandro's mind whirled with questions: Would anyone ever understand? Could they help him untangle the memories and make sense of it all? Or would this darkness forever define him, a perpetual reminder of that one night when everything went wrong?
